static_traits.name: Wang Rui
static_traits.family_status: Living with family; the father works in a factory
static_traits.medical_history: Has not previously received psychotherapy or counseling; no major physical illness; no similar academic problems occurred in the past
static_traits.language_features: Able to clearly describe problems and triggering situations, frequently uses catastrophic statements in expression; attitude rather negative but cooperation relatively high; speech rate not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I am experiencing a significant decline in grades, attributed to time spent on training, which makes me anxious and afraid of failing, losing my scholarship, and eventually working in a factory like my father. These problems progressed rapidly after this semester began and sports commitments increased; strong anxiety appears almost every time before exams or when receiving assignment feedback. I try to compensate for training time by studying late at night, but there has been no improvement.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I realize that anxiety about failure and losing the scholarship is affecting my mental health and academic performance.
growth_experiences: Family of origin and background: lives with family, father works in a factory; in the current distress, the client frequently mentions worry and associations about 'working in a factory like my father'.
Past study and health history: no similar academic problems before; no psychotherapy or counseling received; no major physical illness.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on grades and scholarships
I will fail and lose everything

special_situations.event: Before exams or when receiving assignment feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If this exam or feedback goes badly, it means I am heading toward failure and will lose the scholarship
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Staying up late studying to make up for time taken by training

special_situations.event: At the start of the semester, the sports training schedule becomes busy, compressing study time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do both studies and training well at the same time, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Making up for training time through overtime-style studying, ignoring rest and efficiency
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Practicing more will surely make grades worse and worse

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Continuously declining grades mean eventually dropping out and losing the scholarship
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further increasing study time but with poor results
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will drop out of school and will only be able to work in factories in the future

core_conflict.wish: Longs to maintain achievements and recognition (keeping the scholarship, finding balance between academics and sports)
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure, disappointing others, and ultimately ending up working in a factory like the father with a ruined future
defense_goal: Reduces anxiety and uncertainty and maintains a sense of controllability through doubled effort and emphasizing external causes

object_relations.self_representation: A student who may fail at any time, an individual who needs to constantly prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: Significant others (family, teachers, classmates) are harsh judges and imposers of expectations
object_relations.linking_affect: Anxiety, stress, fear of disappointing others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks for evidence for the worst outcome, or explores the specific factors behind declining grades
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to attribute the problem solely to 'training taking up time', maintaining an explanatory framework for failure anxiety
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses an empathic, gentle tone; first validates their concern, then discusses from concrete facts and a multi-factor perspective; uses open-ended questions to guide them to explore other possible causes in an atmosphere free of negation.

manifestations: Finds it hard to balance and choose between academics and sports, highly worried about the resulting consequences (losing the scholarship, a restricted future)
Narrows the future path to a single option: 'if I fail I can only work in a factory like my father'
outcomes: Impaired sleep (difficulty falling asleep late at night)
Diet and overall health are affected

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently worrying about 'disappointing everyone', over-focusing on the possibility of failure
In sessions, finds it hard to maintain a connection to positive evidence (for example, despite passing the last exam, quickly returns to the worst-case assumption)

exception_events.target_problem: Before exams, the client usually experiences strong anxiety and catastrophically predicts failure, then stays up late studying and is fatigued during the day, causing grades and state to be further affected.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the last exam, the client originally thought he would fail, but ultimately passed the exam; the worst case did not happen, and he experienced some relief and loosening.
exception_events.reason: Clues: factual counter-evidence shows that 'anxiety does not necessarily lead to failure'; the experience of passing this time provided material to correct the catastrophic predictions.

positive_force: Has social support (teammates and friends to talk with)
Able to identify and describe triggering situations and feelings (before exams, anxiety when receiving feedback)
Willing to seek professional help and try cognitive restructuring
Existing positive evidence (having passed an exam when failure was expected)
negative_force: Marked cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, mental filtering, and jumping to conclusions
Stays up late to catch up on studying, causing insufficient sleep and daytime fatigue
Over-tying grades and scholarship to self-worth, worrying about disappointing others
In key academic situations (before exams, feedback), anxiety peaks frequently occur

target_behavior.behavior: Experiences intense anxiety and catastrophic thinking during exams or when receiving homework feedback, and copes by staying up late to study
antecedent: Receiving feedback on assignments or grades
After sports training, less study time and a busier pace
target_behavior.core_reason: Tightly binds grades with scholarships and self-worth, makes catastrophic predictions about the future (dropping out, going to work in a factory); time management is imbalanced.
target_behavior.function: Escapes the fear of failure and gains a brief sense of control and safety (through studying overtime).
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient sleep, daytime fatigue and reduced attention, grades decline further; relationships with classmates are strained; eating and overall health are affected.
